summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with recurrent abdominal pain and nausea/vomiting that returned after eating tacos, following a recent hospital discharge. She reported collapsing at home in her vomit, prompting re-evaluation. CT imaging showed no acute abdominal pathology, consistent with prior unremarkable studies. Pain and nausea were managed with IV fluids, Dilaudid, and Zofran, with gradual advancement to oral intake. Her chronic pancreatitis was considered the likely contributor, though no active inflammation was seen. A mild Sjogren’s flare with facial erythema and low-grade fever was noted but remained asymptomatic. She tolerated a soft diet, had no pain, and was discharged home with instructions to resume all home medications and follow up with her PCP and rheumatologist. H. pylori treatment was deferred pending outpatient coordination.
